evidence.observation: The title resolves first and the orange underline draws left-to-right immediately afterward.
A complete inactive nine-node scaffold is visible before nodes and connectors activate from left to right.
The existing pipeline geometry is preserved while the fault and subsequent path change to danger red.
Rotated scattered tiles translate and rotate into an orthogonal 3×2 modular grid.
AI and human responsibilities are expressed as two color-coded columns with a relation between them.
The headline appears first, then the left conceptual card, then the right browser panel, followed by the result.
Red and green cards are established before a shield is inserted between them as the explanatory relationship.
A centered house illustration replaces the previous abstract scene at a metaphorical explanation beat.
Child cards exist before multiple colored curved dependency connectors become visible behind them.
A green parent container encloses child modules and visually expresses locality and one controlled boundary.
A dark terminal panel is established before a brighter report panel is inserted to its right.
Problem-to-solution mapping rows append downward in narration order without rearranging prior rows.
A completed comparison is dimmed before a large centered verdict callout overlays it.
The conclusion headline is replaced by a white subscribe pill whose internal actions appear later.
Across the opening samples, a dark fixed canvas, top chapter rail, left phase label, central information stage, and bottom caption remain in stable screen regions.
Title and metrics are replaced as one group by a centered portrait-and-identity card.
A centered abstract cube functions as a sparse chapter hero while the fixed chrome remains visible.
A code/file panel remains on screen while a large numeric conclusion is appended on the right.
A second one-problem/one-skill mapping row enters after the first row is already readable.
The recent AI sample uses a flat dark canvas, orange chapter system, geometric information stage, and bottom caption.
Abstract technical content is decomposed into labeled geometric units and directional relationships.
A recent adjacent video retains the top segmented progress treatment and left chapter label.
Orange is reused across outlines, arrows, labels, and focal geometry instead of being only a title color.
The recent tutorial sample shows the same segmented top progress and left chapter marker.
A technical explanation is organized through cards and comparison-oriented spatial grouping.
A real product interface is framed as evidence within the dark explainer layout.
The recent AI sample uses orange as a system accent with restrained secondary colors.
A segmented top rail and chapter label persist over a sparse technical scene.
An illustration is used for a metaphorical explanation within an otherwise information-graphic video.
The related skill video uses the current flat dark-gray and orange card system.
A product UI window and bold bottom caption are integrated without replacing the overall dark layout.
A small circular presenter picture-in-picture sits at lower right while information graphics remain the primary stage.
A code/product panel and a burned-in bottom caption coexist on the dark explainer canvas.
A recipe/kitchen metaphor appears as an occasional illustration-led explanatory scene.
The earlier AI sample uses a dark information-graphic stage with cards and diagrammatic relationships.
The finance-era sample keeps the presenter small while performance and comparison graphics dominate.
Red/green market metrics and valuation-style information are tied to the finance topic.
White bold text and a black bottom caption capsule provide a high-contrast readability skeleton.
The finance-era sample still prioritizes dark information graphics over a full-screen presenter.
The earliest sampled video is a dark information graphic rather than a full-screen talking head.
Even the early finance sample decomposes an explanation into cards, numbers, and directional relationships.
This early finance sample uses a dense neon HUD, grid, glow, and several competing saturated colors.

rules.claim: Use a dark, information-first canvas; a presenter must not replace the explanatory stage.
Use bold high-contrast sans text and a separate black bottom-caption capsule as the readability skeleton.
Translate abstract technical content into cards, nodes, arrows, containment, or side-by-side comparison before adding decoration.
For the current AI-explainer era, use flat dark gray with orange as the structural accent and keep secondary semantic colors sparse.
For recent AI-series work, retain the segmented top progress rail and left chapter marker as fixed navigation chrome.
Represent a narrated ordered process as a complete inactive horizontal scaffold, then activate it in reading order.
When narration changes state without changing the conceptual model, preserve geometry and mutate border, fill, connector, glow, or status color.
Represent small, editable, composable units by moving scattered tiles into an orthogonal modular grid.
Build comparisons progressively: establish the claim, reveal the first side, reveal the second side, then append the result or verdict.
In the target, orange marks current focus, red marks failure or harmful propagation, and green marks pass, completion, or containment.
Keep navigation chrome and captions independent from the replaceable SceneStage so scene motion does not displace them.
Use real product, browser, terminal, or report UI as occasional demonstration evidence inside the dark layout, not as the default geometry for every beat.
Use illustration as an occasional metaphor or abstraction reset while retaining the surrounding explainer system.
If an older-era presenter picture-in-picture is used, keep it small and subordinate to the information graphic.
Exclude dense neon HUD, glowing grids, and finance-specific red/green metric cards from the current AI-explainer baseline unless the user explicitly requests that era or topic.
rules.limits: This exclusion is based on a 15-video stratified sample and style evolution across those samples; it does not prove that no later upload ever reuses a legacy motif.

rules.claim: Sequence a target-style explanatory scene as establish scaffold, focus current relation, mutate state, then append the explanation or verdict.
Treat pixel dimensions and spring values from the 01:49–02:16 reconstruction as segment-local calibration, then remeasure other scenes from their cited frames.
rules.limits: The rendered video does not expose the creator's source project, global tokens, or easing curves; only the calibrated replica segment has exact implementation values.

rules.claim: Use short deterministic opacity, translation, color, line-draw, or settling-spring changes to reproduce the observed direction, while labeling exact easing and font choices as approximations.
rules.limits: Four-frame strips establish order and visible property changes but cannot uniquely recover every original keyframe, cubic-bezier, font file, or asset type.
